description:
The exhaustive record assertion, and the successful counterpart of case18. A re-entry on ENTER with 'ADMIN005' and 'PASSWORD' - the identical screenRequest case18 declares, differing in one respect only: case18 forces the read at :211-219 onto its OTHER outcome, and this case lets it succeed. Pairing the two isolates the I/O outcome as the single variable behind the whole divergence, so a translation that reached the right answer here for the wrong reason - by ignoring WS-RESP-CD rather than by matching WHEN 0 - cannot pass both. Both fields are already upper case, so FUNCTION UPPER-CASE at :132 and :135 is the identity here and the key is unchanged by it; WS-ERR-FLG is still 'N' at :138, so READ-USER-SEC-FILE is performed; the read returns normally and EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD matches its first ordered arm, WHEN 0 at :222; the plaintext comparison at :223 succeeds; :224-228 populates the communication area; and because SEC-USR-TYPE is 'A', CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is true and :230-232 names COADM01C. Where the other nineteen cases pin the record they touch, this one is the folder's byte-complete decode of an 80-byte CSUSR01Y record, and it is the case that carries the record-width and FILLER gates.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80. Summed mechanically from the copybook, span by span: SEC-USR-ID PIC X(08) at offset 0, length 8, ending 7; SEC-USR-FNAME PIC X(20) at 8, length 20, ending 27; SEC-USR-LNAME PIC X(20) at 28, length 20, ending 47; SEC-USR-PWD PIC X(08) at 48, length 8, ending 55; SEC-USR-TYPE PIC X(01) at 56, length 1, ending 56 - which is 57, exactly the width of the seed rows - then SEC-USR-FILLER PIC X(23) at 57, length 23, ending 79, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and is never hand-padded here. Row 4 is decoded in full because it is the widest-name row of the ten - 'GRANVILLE' is 9 characters and 'LACHAPELLE' is 10 - so its padding arithmetic is the least likely of any row to come out right by accident: SEC-USR-ID is 'ADMIN005' at its full 8; SEC-USR-FNAME is 'GRANVILLE' followed by 11 spaces, 20 in all; SEC-USR-LNAME is 'LACHAPELLE' followed by 10 spaces, 20 in all; SEC-USR-PWD is 'PASSWORD' at its full 8; SEC-USR-TYPE is 'A', 1; and SEC-USR-FILLER is 23 spaces. Those six lengths are 8, 20, 20, 8, 1 and 23, which total exactly 80, and the 80-character expectedBytes image alongside them states that total independently of the field map. SEC-USR-FILLER is named in that map rather than left out because CSUSR01Y.cpy:23 names it - it is a declared 05-level item, not an anonymous gap - and a record serialised without it is short by precisely 23 bytes, collapsing from 80 to 57 and displacing every offset that follows. Nothing is trimmed: PIC X values are space-padded on the wire and COSGN00C nowhere trims them, so the padding runs are part of the expectation rather than noise to be normalised away. The same job corroborates the target width twice more, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster, and SecUserRecord states it a fourth time as RECORD_LENGTH with KEY_OFFSET 0 and KEY_LENGTH 8. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record; the ten expectedFinalState images therefore also assert that the file came back unaltered. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0.

Nothing is sent. :230-232 transfers control, so SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN at :145-157 is not performed and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :177-204 is never reached. There is consequently no ERRMSGO and no map-field projection to pin at all - CURDATEO, CURTIMEO, APPLIDO, SYSIDO, TITLE01O and TITLE02O are absent from this case not by omission but because the paragraph that assigns them does not run - and sends is empty while nextMapset, nextMap and cursorField are all unstated, since :230-239 hands the client a program name rather than a screen and contains no MOVE -1. expectedMessages is empty for the same reason and because COSGN00C has no DISPLAY on any path. The clock is pinned regardless, at 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so that no timezone can shift it and no wall-clock reading can enter: it is declared for consistency with the other nineteen cases even though the CURRENT-DATE at :179 is unreachable here. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds; on this path those two substitutions are likewise unobservable, and that is stated rather than papered over with values the run never produces. The charset is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout and its six offsets, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the 160-byte communication area, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00 and its PROGRAM(COSGN00C), and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path, so the decision at :223 is reached directly. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. The password stays plaintext: SEC-USR-PWD PIC X(08) is stored as 'PASSWORD' in the record and compared in plaintext because app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:223 compares it in plaintext. That is an inherited property of the legacy design and an explicit non-goal of this migration, stated plainly here rather than obscured, and the eight bytes are compared exactly as stored, with no transformation applied on either side of the comparison and no credential-protection scheme introduced by this migration. Two absences are worth recording rather than quietly assuming: app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7 and is therefore a COBOL comment, so no DFHATTR constant applies to this program at all; and COSGN00C copies CSSETATY nowhere, so the DFHRED-plus-asterisk error highlight that CSSETATY provides its one consumer has no counterpart on any path here, which is why no attribute item is pinned. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked.
